newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Pope tells Hungarians to be patient in hard times.
newsitem.headline: Pope tells Hungarians to be patient in hard times.

text.p: Pope John Paul said on arrival in Hungary on Friday for a two-day visit that the people of Hungary needed patience during painful times after regaining their freedom from dictatorship.

"The optimism linked to the historic fall of ideology has unfortunately been very short-lived," he told an audience at Hungary's Ferihegy airport. "It has been replaced by a troublesome period of difficulty which in Hungary has marked and continues to mark the life of everyone."
The 76-year-old Pontiff, speaking in both Hungarian and English, said the people of Hungary must not be discouraged.
"After the tragic events of this century which is coming to an end we should not be surprised if the rebirth and hoped-for development require time," he said.

"The disastrous consequences of the long years of dictatorship can be overcome materially and spritually only with patient and persevering commitment on the part of everyone, especially the younger generation."
The Pope spoke clearly from his podium on the airport tarmac, concentrating intently on his Hungarian notes.
Earlier he had looked in reasonable health as he walked steadily down the steps of the Alitalia plane and was greeted under unusually chilly grey skies by Hungarian President Arpad Goncz.
Two girls presented him with flowers in the Vatican colours of yellow and white.
He did not kiss the ground, a regular feature of his trips, as he had already visited Hungary in 1991.

The Pope, who hopes to lead the Roman Catholic Church into the third millennium, is to attend a ceremony on Friday to mark the 1,000th anniversary of a Benedictine monastery at Pannonhalma in western Hungary.
On Saturday he celebrates a huge outdoor mass in the nearby city of Gyor, on the River Danube, and meets Hungarian bishops before returning to Rome that evening.
The trip, the Pope's 73rd abroad, follows a fresh scare about his health in mid-August when he entered hospital briefly for a battery of sophisticated medical tests.
